title: A synovial joint lets bones move against each other
summary: OpenStax says a synovial joint lets bones move freely against each other, with cartilage and a slick coating.
body: OpenStax says synovial joints are the most common joints. The bone surfaces are not fastened directly together. They meet inside the joint and can move freely. Articular cartilage and a slick coating cut friction. Ligaments hold the bones together and resist excessive movement. A freely movable joint of this kind is called a diarthrosis. The elbow is a hinge example on the page. This card is how a movable joint is built. It is not care for a twisted joint.

sources.title: 9.1 and 9.4, chapter review
sources.author: OpenStax
sources.note: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology, first edition, web view, CC BY 4.0. Paraphrase: synovial joints have a fluid-filled cavity, articular cartilage, synovial fluid, and ligaments; they are diarthroses, freely movable.
